Some instances carry an explicit parenthetical harness/color label, e.g. '(R)', '(B) (MINI)', '(G)', '[MINI]'.

connector_count_reconciliation.finding: Direct raster inspection, applying the given engineering definition, found 10 distinct instances of the diagram's consistent inline-connector symbol convention in a partial sweep of the diagram (Alarm Unit, CDI Unit, the relay cluster, the Pulse Generator/Reverse Switch area, and the tail-light/fuse area) - MORE than the manually-reported 8, and further locations near the Ignition Switch, Rectifier, Regulator/Rectifier, Battery/Starter Relay, and headlight/indicator harnesses were not exhaustively checked and may contain additional instances.
connector_count_reconciliation.possible_grouping_interpretation: conn-03/conn-04 (CDI) and conn-05/conn-06 (Alarm Unit) each appear as adjacent twin housings serving one component's harness and could plausibly be counted by a human reviewer as one physical connector location each rather than two, which would reduce the found count toward 8 (10 -> 8 if both pairs are merged). This is a plausible but UNCONFIRMED interpretation - this audit does not assert it as fact.
connector_count_reconciliation.conclusion: This audit could not uniquely and confidently map its raster findings to the specific 8 locations the manual count refers to. The pin-count-only total observed across the 10 found instances is 2+2+4+2+3+2+4+3+3+3 = 28 (counting each instance's one-side pin count, i.e. number of wires passing through) - this does not cleanly reconcile with 46 under any counting convention tried (28 as-is, or 56 if doubled for both sides), which independently confirms that either additional connector locations exist beyond the 10 found, or per-connector pin counts were undercounted in this pass, or both. Per this AP's own instruction, this discrepancy is reported rather than resolved by assumption.

terminal_count_validation.reason: The 46 total cannot be independently reconstructed from current model artifacts (0 ConnectorCandidates/ConnectorTerminals exist) or from this audit's partial raster sweep (10 locations, 28 one-side pins, not exhaustive). Stated explicitly per this task's own instruction rather than invented.

opposing_side_test.result: All 10 found instances show entry on one side/end and exit on the directly opposing side/end (top/bottom for vertical harness runs, left/right for the two relay-cluster boxes), with wire-color labels preserved across the connector confirming pass-through rather than component transformation. This was verified visually per-instance (drawn wire-color labels on both sides), not inferred from the bounding box shape alone.
opposing_side_test.caveat: The current extraction model does not preserve terminal side/orientation or a connector axis for any of these 9 candidateless locations, since no ComponentCandidate/geometry exists for them at all. For conn-01 (the one with a ComponentCandidate), the model's TerminalCandidate/EndpointCandidate records carry position but no explicit 'side' or 'axis' attribute - side/opposition was determined by this audit from direct raster inspection, not from any model field.

conductor_entry_exit_test.result: For conn-01 only (the sole candidate with model representation): 2 ConductorSegments/topology edges connect to it, and 2 physical Wires (wire-0a3ab2e5ace89210, wire-e5f7ff766561e9b7) terminate at its 2 endpoints - this is model-represented conductor continuity up to the connector's own boundary on each side, though the model does not represent 'continuity THROUGH the connector' as a single concept - each side's Wire simply ends at its own endpoint, exactly as AP-WIRE-029 defines a hard Wire boundary. For the other 9 locations, no ConductorSegment, topology node, or Wire references them at all, because no ComponentCandidate/geometry exists there to anchor such evidence - not because the underlying conductor ink is absent (direct raster inspection confirms real, continuous ink entering and leaving every one of the 10 locations).

inline_test.result: All 10 found instances sit within a conductor path with drawn ink continuing on both sides (never at a page edge with only one side connected), consistent with the 'inline' requirement. The AP-DIAG-AUDIT-009 'OPTIONAL' P/G plug symbol (~800,270) was also inspected and explicitly EXCLUDED from this list: it has only one open, unterminated end (an accessory pigtail) and therefore fails the conductor-exit / non-outer-edge-termination requirement - correctly distinguished from a true inline connector per the task's own Connector Boundary Rule.

outer_edge_negative_test.result: None of the 10 found instances are located at the outer boundary of the page/drawing area. All sit well within the interior wiring, with conductors entering and exiting on both sides. The one symbol that IS an outer/dead-end termination (the 'OPTIONAL' P/G plug) was correctly excluded, not misclassified as a connector on the basis of proximity or terminal presence alone.

Not a component body, not an annotation.

Not consistent with a lamp, relay-coil-zigzag, diode-triangle, ground-bar, or switch-circle symbol (all independently characterized in AP-DIAG-AUDIT-008/008B). Strong connector evidence per the given definition (opposing terminals, conductor entry+exit, inline position); none of it is model-represented for these 9.

crossing_rules_compliance: No connector identification in this audit relied on a diagonal wire, a direction change at an intersection, an X-crossing transfer, or treating a crossing as a splice/endpoint. All opposing-side/pass-through observations were made directly from drawn wire-color labels and connector symbol geometry, independent of topology-node classification.

answers.q1_all_eight_located: Not confirmed as exactly eight. Ten distinct instances of the connector symbol convention were found in a partial sweep; several additional diagram areas were not exhaustively checked.
answers.q2_terminal_counts_per_connector: conn-01=2, conn-02=2, conn-03=4, conn-04=2, conn-05=3, conn-06=2, conn-07=4, conn-08=3, conn-09=3, conn-10=3 (one-side pin counts, i.e. number of wires passing through each).
answers.q3_total_equals_46: No - the 10 found instances sum to 28 one-side pins, not 46. Cannot be reconciled from current evidence; either more locations exist, some pin counts were undercounted, or both.
answers.q4_opposing_side_rule_satisfied: Yes for all 10 found instances, verified by direct raster inspection of preserved wire-color labels on both sides.
answers.q5_conductor_entry_exit_evidence: Yes for all 10 as raster ink; only conn-01 has this represented in the extraction model (ConductorSegment/topology/Wire).
answers.q6_current_extraction_preserves_evidence: No for 9 of 10 - no model representation exists at all. Partial for conn-01 - conductor evidence is preserved as ordinary ComponentBoundary terminals/Wires, not connector-specific evidence.
answers.q7_terminals_represented_as_another_type: Yes for conn-01's 7 terminals (represented as ComponentBoundary TerminalCandidates / component_terminal EndpointCandidates). No representation of any kind exists for the other 9 locations' terminals.
answers.q8_classified_as_enclosure: No - conn-01 is classified CircularSymbol; the other 9 were never classified at all (no candidate exists). The premise that connectors are being misclassified as Enclosure is not supported by this diagram's evidence.
answers.q9_connectorboundary_primitivesymbol_com: No. The one confirmed genuine connector in the model (conn-01) has ShapeKind Circle, which ComponentCandidateClassifier unconditionally maps to CircularSymbol - never PrimitiveSymbol, which is only reachable from a non-enclosure Rectangle. Even if a PrimitiveSymbol-kind candidate existed elsewhere, this specific real connector's own shape family would still never satisfy the current ConnectorBoundary condition, because that condition depends on a shape family (Rectangle) this diagram's actual connector symbols (rounded/notched boxes and ovals) do not consistently use.
answers.q10_primary_failure_layer: A combination, with upstream ShapeDetector/geometry classification dominant: for 9 of 10 found locations, no ComponentCandidate is ever proposed at all (upstream geometry/shape-detection gap, prior to any terminal or connector logic). For the 1 location that does have a candidate, the failure is connector-boundary architecture: the ConnectorBoundary condition is keyed to a ComponentCandidateKind (PrimitiveSymbol, itself keyed to a specific ShapeRole) that does not match this diagram's actual connector-symbol shape family (Circle/notched-oval), not a missing-terminal or missing-conductor-evidence problem for that one candidate.
answers.q11_identity_without_ocr: Partially. The opposing-side/pass-through/wire-color-preservation pattern is establishable from geometry and existing conductor-color labels alone (no OCR needed) for the connector's EXISTENCE and boundary. The parenthetical labels seen on some instances ('(R)', '(B) (MINI)', '[MINI] (G)') would require OCR to read as identifying strings, but are not needed to establish that a pass-through connector interface exists at that location.
answers.q12_hypothetical_production_change: IF this audit's findings were to be acted on (not done here): (a) ShapeDetector/ComponentCandidateClassifier would need a shape-family rule recognizing the notched/interlocking pass-through symbol (rounded-rect or oval with a step-notch or staircase split) as its own ComponentCandidateKind, independent of the existing Circle/Rectangle/Enclosure buckets, since neither current bucket reliably captures it; (b) the ConnectorBoundary terminal-kind condition in terminal_location_detector.cpp/terminal_recognizer.cpp would need to key off that new kind instead of (or in addition to) PrimitiveSymbol; (c) opposing-side wire-color preservation could then serve as corroborating, non-OCR evidence for ConnectorTerminalModelBuilder. This is a description of the evidence gap only - no such change was made.
